code_safety.reason: scored on the declared repository, because the published package carries its code only as build output, which is not read as the server's own source; no tag matched this version, so the repository's default branch was read and the findings describe that code, not necessarily the release

evidence.label: mcp-js-ssrf-nonliteral-url (medium/low)
evidence.detail: An outbound request is made to a URL that is not a literal. If any part is caller-supplied the server can be aimed at internal hosts it can reach and the caller cannot.

evidence.label: authentication_model
evidence.detail: stdio transport: the client launches the server as a subprocess, so the OS process boundary is the auth boundary — `03` §4 does not penalise absent auth here

evidence.label: transport_security
evidence.detail: declared transport: stdio — launched as a subprocess by the client, so the security boundary is the client process, not a network port (`03` §4)

evidence.label: secret_handling
evidence.detail: source was fetched but every file in it was oversized, unreadable or excluded, so no source text could be read, so there is nothing to scan for committed credentials

evidence.label: authorization_granularity
evidence.detail: source was fetched but every file in it was oversized, unreadable or excluded, so no source text could be read, so neither the tool count nor any access-control logic can be read

evidence.label: issue_responsiveness
evidence.detail: this repository has no issues `03` §5's window covers. An unanswered issue scores 0 under §5, but a repository with no issues filed has not failed to answer one.

evidence.label: release_cadence
evidence.detail: a release exists but fewer than two fall inside `03` §5's 12-month window, so no median gap can be taken — and §5's remaining bands are all defined on that median. A limit of the methodology, not of this repository.

evidence.label: repository_signals
evidence.detail: `03` §5 scores this by quartile WITHIN the server's category, which needs a distribution across every scanned server and so cannot be computed while scanning one. It is a post-pass over the crawl and that pass does not exist yet.

dependency_health.reason: no lockfile in the published package (npm does not publish a package's package-lock.json; npm-shrinkwrap.json is the lockfile a published package can carry); dependency versions are unresolved, so no vulnerability can be attributed

evidence.label: license
evidence.detail: LICENSE present with no SPDX-License-Identifier tag; identified as 'MIT' from its text

evidence.label: readme_quality
evidence.detail: README.md: installation instructions (+25), configuration documented (+25), exposed tools or resources enumerated (+30), states what the server does in the first 200 words (+20)

evidence.label: declared_scopes
evidence.detail: specific scope or access documentation is present, but `03` §7's 100 and 60 bands both compare it against scopes INFERRED from static analysis, which is not built yet. Scoring 100 on an empty inference would be a vacuous truth — 'all ∅ inferred scopes are documented'.

evidence.label: changelog
evidence.detail: no CHANGELOG in the fetched source. `03` §7's partial credit for tagged releases carrying release notes is not applied here — that needs the forge API, which this check does not call

install_resolution.label: Resolved by deps.dev, not read from a lockfile the publisher shipped: these are the versions deps.dev's resolver picked for an install of this package, which can differ from what a real install picks. deps.dev records no resolution time and has been measured lagging the npm registry by up to about 30 hours.
